newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A Makati City judge issues an arrest order for congressman Romeo Jalosjos of Zamboanga del Norte in southern Philippines on charges of two counts of statutory rape and 12 counts of acts of lasciviousness. Police, however, are still unable to locate the congressman. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Prime Minister Sheikh Khalifa Bun Salman Al Khalifa of Bahrain arrives with 10 high-ranking Bahraini government officials and nine businessmen for a four-day visit. (BULLETIN)
- President Fidel Ramos returns to work after checking out of hospital. (PHILIPPINE STAR/CHRONICLE)

- Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson says ceiling on domestic borrowings of foreign companies set to be lifted starting January 1997 to provide foreign firms more leeway to raise funds. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Petron Corp signs memorandum of agreement with Ssangyong Oil Refining Co Ltd early this week to undertake a feasibility study to build an aromatics-oriented grassroots oil refinery. (BUSINESSWORLD/MANILA TIME)

- The National Development Co and Hottick Investments Ltd, the new controlling stockholder of the National Steel Corp (NSC), have agreed to offer at least 12.5 percent of NSC's shares to the public next year. (BUSINESS DAILY) - The Central Bank expects the country's overall balance of payments to yield a surplus of $4 billion by yearend, an improvement from the meager $631 million surplus posted in 1995. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co and other local exchange carriers are set to file a 100 peso increase in monthly basic telephone charges January 1997. (MANILA BULLETIN/MANILA TIMES)

- The Central Bank expects an eight percent economic growth and a six percent inflation level next year if current reforms and prudent policies of the government stay on course. (TIMES JOURNAL/PHILIPPINE STAR/CHRONICLE)
